record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.context_brief: Algorithmic recognition of isohedral polycube tilings
record.original_question: Let a polycube be a strongly connected union of axis-aligned unit cubes on the cubic lattice. Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether a given polycube admits an isohedral tiling of three-dimensional space?

evidence.quote: The three-dimensional analogs of polyominoes are polycubes: subsets of R3 formed by strongly connected unions of axis-aligned unit cubes centered at locations on the cubic lattice Z3. Just as polyominoes tile the plane, polycubes may tile three-dimensional space.
Open Problem 3 Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for determining whether a polycube has an isohedral tiling?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polycube is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ formed by a strongly connected union of finitely many axis-aligned closed unit cubes centered at points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^3$ (strong connectivity meaning that the union remains connected after removing all cubes' shared edges and vertices, i.e., adjacent cubes share a full 2-dimensional face). A tiling of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of a polycube $P$ is a covering of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by isometric copies of $P$ with pairwise disjoint interiors. Such a tiling is called isohedral if its symmetry group acts transitively on the tiles; equivalently, for any two tiles there is an isometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$ that preserves the tiling globally and maps one tile to the other.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input a polycube $P$ (described, say, by the list of lattice positions of its constituent unit cubes), decides in time polynomial in the number of unit cubes of $P$ whether $P$ admits an isohedral tiling of $\mathbb{R}^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: For the 2D analogue (polyominoes), Keating–Vince and later Langerman–Winslow gave polynomial- and quasilinear-time algorithms for isohedral tilings of the plane. No analogous polynomial-time algorithm for polycubes deciding isohedral tilings of 3-space appears in the literature found; the 3D case remains stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A Quasilinear-Time Algorithm for Tiling the Plane Isohedrally with a Polyomino
status_evidence.snippet: O(n log^2 n) algorithm for isohedral plane tiling by polyominoes, improving Keating–Vince.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time results exist for the 2D polyomino case, but the 3D polycube case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Isohedral Polyomino Tiling of the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for isohedral tiling of the plane by a polyomino.
status_evidence.claim: Existing polynomial-time isohedral tiling algorithms are confined to the planar polyomino setting.
